children.translated_text: With “In the ocean [I set] you,” he sets afloat the jar of Soma dregs.
Having released it, he reverentially approaches with “Divine waters...”
With “<s>Avabhṛtha</s>,” he submerges it.

children.text: kṛṣṇājināntaṃ ca mā maindryaṃ jyaiṣṭhyaṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ vyauṣīr iti putrāyainat pradāya varuṇapraghāsavat snānaprabhṛty ā samidādhānāt ||
children.translated_text: Having given that black antelope skin to his son with the words, “Do not separate from me my Indra-like power, seniority, and preeminence,” the procedure is as in the <s>Varuṇapraghāsa</s>, from the bath through the placing of kindling on the fire.
He casts away that which is smeared with Soma.
In the first two cases there is no giving away.

children.text: ud vayam ity unnetronnītā āmahīyāṃ japanto gacchanti apāma somam amṛtā abhūma aganma jyotir avidāma devān kiṃ nūnam asmān kṛṇavad arātiḥ kim u dhūrtir amṛta martyasya iti ||
children.translated_text: Those led by the <s>Unnetṛ</s> proceed, reciting “Up we...” and the <s>Āmahīya</s>: “We have drunk Soma and become immortal; we have reached the light and found the gods. What can hostility now do to us? What can mortal malice do, O immortal one?”
The sacrificer sits west of the <s>Śālādvārya</s> fire, placing the black antelope skin in his lap.

children.text: sruvāhutiṃ juhoti maindryaṃ jyaiṣṭhyaṃ śraiṣṭhyam agnir dadhātu svāhā iti ||
children.translated_text: He offers a ladle-oblation with the words, “May <s>Agni</s> establish in me Indra-like power, seniority, and preeminence. Svāhā!”
After putting down the black antelope skin, he performs the <s>Udayanīya</s> offering in the same manner as the <s>Prāyaṇīya</s>.
<s>Pathyā Svasti</s> is the fourth deity.

children.text: pātraprokṣaṇādy ājyāsādanāt savanīyavat parivyayaṇādi maitrāvaruṇī vaśānūbandhyā ||
children.translated_text: From the sprinkling of the vessels through the setting down of the ghee, the procedure is as at the <s>Savanīya</s> sacrifice; from the girding onward, the barren cow for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> is the concluding animal.
Alternatively, one may begin with the insertion of the <s>svaru</s> (wooden splinter), since the preceding rites have already been performed.
If there is no barren cow, a bull is used.
If neither is available, a <s>payasyā</s> (curds-and-whey offering) is used.
Some, after setting her in place, perform the rites from the two ghee-portions through the <s>Iḍā</s>.
The concluding offering is a five-potsherd cake for <s>Agni</s>, made on the fire produced by friction after the sacred fires have been transferred.
Gold is the sacrificial fee.
Or it is a draught ox.
Alternatively, the oblation is performed as at an animal sacrifice.
At its conclusion comes the evening offering.
It is an ancillary part of the Soma sacrifice, on account of proximity and conflict.
Alternatively, the morning offering is obligatory, because scripture expressly mentions the morning offering.
This follows from the prescribed regularity of the rite.
This is the first form of the Soma sacrifice.
After kindling the fires, they enter.
The following six come after it.
They are the <s>Atyagniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Ukthya</s>, <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, <s>Vājapeya</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>, and <s>Aptoryāma</s>.

children.text: teṣām ukthyo 'chāvākam abhi saṃtiṣṭhate hotāram itare ||
children.translated_text: Of these, the <s>Ukthya</s> terminates with the <s>Acchāvāka</s>; the others terminate with the <s>Hotṛ</s>.

children.text: vaiśyarājanyayoḥ some nyagrodhastibhīn upanahyechan bhakṣāya krayaṇaprabhṛty anusomam āvṛtā samānam āsādanaṃ prāg abhiṣavāt ||
children.translated_text: At a Soma sacrifice for a <s>Vaiśya</s> or a <s>Rājanya</s>, one should bind up bunches of banyan material intended for consumption. From the purchase onward, the procedure follows that of the Soma sacrifice; their setting down is the same and takes place before the pressing.
At the time when the cups are filled, he should bring the material, mix it thoroughly with curds, and have that cup filled in sequence.

children.text: hūyamāneṣu kuśataruṇena juhoti ahaṃ tvad asmi iti ||
children.translated_text: While the oblations are being offered, he makes the offering with a tender shoot of <s>kuśa</s> grass, saying, “I am from you.”
